It is a lot like what Finishing School is (I believe that's more of a European title for it). It can also be called Cotillion classes (Cotillions are big "coming out" balls much in a way that quinceaneras are to present a Latina girl as a woman and bat mitzvahs are to present a Jewish girl. Cotillions were originally thought of as a Greek tradition but have become popular among all nationalities. Traditionally they happen as a girl's "Sweet 16" but it's becoming increasingly common to hold off on the actual Cotillion for their 18th birthday, although they will still have a sweet 16 party). Some parents choose basic etiquette classes when their child is around 8 - 10 just for basic manners and such and then that's it. Some are increasingly thorough and cover all areas of life. These are the kind I participated in.

I took classes (as did my sister) in an increasing way. It goes in an assending set of classes. At ages 4, 6, 8 and 10 we had 8 classes at each age that were 1 hour long per class. At age 12, just before we turned 13, we had 4 special classes that were 2 hours long. In preparation for turning 16, we had aseries of 8 classes, 4 hours long each, and the end was our Sweet 16 party. When we turned 18 there was a set of 12 classes, 4 hours long each. Most chose to take a set 12 classes (4 hours each) when we turned 21 as well.

The basic ideal (and every program is different) is that with each age range of classes, you learn more skills based on where you should be in life. For example, the ones that we took at 16 were based around work opportunities and how to network and communicate within the business world,. At 13, most were based around formal settings (formal dinners, parties, parent's work events) as well as relationships. The set when you turn 21 is based around both alcohol etiquette (as we are in America) and building deeper personal professional relationships because, at 21, most people are graduating their first round of college. Marriage is usually touched on briefly in the pre-16 classes and then highly explored in the ones you take when you're 18 and 21.

Ours were run by a True Southern Belle who was born and raised with the old fashioned styles of things so it was intriguing. Some things have changed over the years and were taught accordingly but for the most part we were taught very in depthly the basics you would expecting: Table setting, dress codes, first impressions. Of course we were also taught personal skills: makeup and hair, dress, the proper walking, ect. There's also a lot of emphasis on speaking techniques, diction, dialect, ect. Fascinating really. I thoroughly enjoyed it.
